### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/doc.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/doc.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b209e0326875aa4c1a63bc0e8cd14c34db03efff` — the merge of head `e4a5898dee9d3f85b3756d01867501bcdcd50e5c` into base `0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b209e0326875aa4c1a63bc0e8cd14c34db03efff && git checkout b209e0326875aa4c1a63bc0e8cd14c34db03efff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b e4a5898dee9d3f85b3756d01867501bcdcd50e5c && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b && git merge --no-ff e4a5898dee9d3f85b3756d01867501bcdcd50e5c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d45c0e71f0a03bdcf2230901515c2a29716a92b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bce0389763c9193e6bdc5356b8995fb6831f9816`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/doc.json, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`resolveDocsAudience.readableTree`, `audienceBooksOf`, `createMetaBookTreeAnswer`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts and packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (both transports' `listTreeInput`), packages/spec/src/system/book.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts, .changeset/27091-book-tree-sibling-claims.md, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/doc-draft.ts (`resolvePlacements`), packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.test.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/DocPage.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/BookPage.tsx

Reviewed against GitHub (PR object, file list, net diff `origin/main` `d745bb5e`...`bce03897`, the head's check-runs read to completion), card #27091 (body, triage 6461914073, claim 6468704954, amendment 6470220479, os-dev-report 6470190013), ADR-0046 §6.4 and §6.7, and #20980. Not against the dev's own report. Head at review start = PR head `bce03897`; one commit on the branch, no later commits.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Signature `resolveBookTree(book, docs, bookPackage?, books?)` — additive, right.** One optional trailing parameter typed `readonly AudienceBook[]` (an interface this module already exports). No export added, none removed or renamed; every 2- and 3-argument call compiles unchanged. The api-surface snapshot (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json:863`, `resolveBookTree (function)`) records existence only, so no regenerated artifact is owed and none is in the diff; `Spec property liveness` on the head is `success`.
2. **The orphan pass only ever shrinks — right.** The sole behavioural edit is one extra conjunct on the orphan filter: `!claimed.has(d.name) && !claimedByAnyBook?.has(d.name)`, followed by the unchanged #20980 own-packages scope test. Nothing is added to any authored group, no entry is created, no group gains a doc. An `audience`-gated sibling's docs leave this book's catch-all and appear nowhere new (pinned: spec test 3 asserts every doc with `books` was a doc without it, in both books).
3. **Without `books` the tree is byte-identical — right.** `claimedByAnyBook` is `undefined`, `undefined?.has(x)` is `undefined`, `!undefined` is `true`, so the filter reduces to the pre-PR predicate. Spec test 5 pins `JSON.stringify` equality for a single-book package, with `[userManual]` as `books` and with none.
4. **The §6.7 audience union is unmoved — right, and pinned.** `resolveBookClaimedDocs` still calls `resolveBookTree(book, docs, bookPackage)` with THREE arguments and skips `UNCATEGORIZED_KEY`, so the claim set is computed exactly as before and never reads the catch-all. `resolveDocAudiences` is refactored onto the `claimsPerBook` generator: same books, same order, same `resolveBookClaimedDocs(book, docs, book.packageId)` per book, same union; a pure extraction. Spec test 4 pins the full audience map over both books plus a stray doc, and that each book's claim set equals its tree's authored entries. The pre-existing `resolveDocAudiences — union over claiming books (§6.7)` describe is untouched.
5. **One judge, no recursion — right.** `resolveBookTree(…, books)` → `claimedByBooks` → `claimsPerBook` → `resolveBookClaimedDocs` → `resolveBookTree` with 3 args → no `claimedByBooks`. Terminates; the orphan pass and the audience union read one claim set.
6. **A doc no book claims still rolls up — right.** Spec test 2 (`crm_stray` under *Uncategorized* in both books); REST test (`loose_note` in both `org_book` and `gated_book` trees for a holder of every set).
7. **REST `readableTree` passes the right list — right, both transports.** `books` is the `audienceBooksOf(...)` list (each book carrying `packageId: b._packageId`), the same list `bookNamed` matches on and `resolveDocAudiences` unions over; `claimsPerBook` reads `book.packageId`, consistent with the `book._packageId` the route passes as `bookPackage`. `RestServer` (`meta-item-read-routes.ts:395`) and the runtime dispatcher (`runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:1153`) both answer through `createMetaBookTreeAnswer`, so one edit fixes the route on both transports. The translated `served` book is what `readableTree` resolves (labels only; membership keys are untouched by translation) — unchanged by this PR.
8. **Implicit per-package book (unknown name) — unchanged.** `bookNamed` derives a book that is not in `books`; its single `include: '*'` group scoped to the package already claims every package doc, so its catch-all was empty before and stays empty.
9. **Every in-repo caller, judged:** `packages/rest` `readableTree` — passes `books`, fixed. `packages/rest` `readablePages` — `resolveBookClaimedDocs`, unchanged by design. `packages/spec` `resolveBookClaimedDocs` — 3 args by design (item 5). `ui/packages/app-shell` `doc-draft.ts:170` `resolvePlacements` — 3 args; it keeps `tree.groups.slice(0, book.spine.groups.length)`, so the catch-all never reaches its answer: unaffected, right. `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.test.ts:236` — single-book test, unaffected, right. `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-book.test.ts:94` — 2 args, unaffected. **Console port `ui/apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.ts:186`** — a separate implementation, called with 2 args by `DocPage.tsx:165` and `BookPage.tsx:52`; at this head it still judges "claimed" per book, so the console sidebar keeps this card's symptom for a holder of both books, and its line-18 sentence "a faithful local port of the framework's `resolveBookTree`" is false at this head. The seat's amendment 6470220479 orders it fixed in this PR as a later commit, so it is recorded here as a **carried item**, not a FAIL of this head (see ③).
10. **Docblocks — true.** `resolveBookTree`'s docblock states the new rule (orphan = of the book's packages AND claimed by no book in `books`), the judge (`resolveBookClaimedDocs` per book), the shrink-only property, the §6.7 invariant and the no-`books` fallback; each sentence matches the code read. `readableTree`'s docblock ("only the docs NO book of this audience claims") is exact for the list the route builds.
11. **Liveness `doc.json` — true.** The `tags` evidence now quotes `resolveBookTree(book, docs, book._packageId, books)`, which is line 710 of `meta-item-read-gate.ts` verbatim; grade unchanged (`live`); the `Spec property liveness` check-run is `success`.
12. **`?package=` scoping — acceptable, not a defect; the body's note is incomplete.** Both transports hand `scopedPackageId` to BOTH `listTreeInput('book', …)` and `listTreeInput('doc', …)`, so under `?package=X` the books of X judge X's docs, and the docs listed are X's: the answer is X's self-consistent view, and the card's target ("another registered book of the same package") is met in full. Without `?package=` every book judges. Two cross-package claim shapes do not judge under a scoped read: (a) a doc of X whose explicit `group` names a group of a book of another package — the shape the PR body names; (b) a book of another package whose group carries `package: 'X'` with an `include` over X's docs — not named in the body. Both are pre-existing scoping semantics of the route (#6877, #20980), not introduced here, and neither widens anything. Should-fix (prose only): the Acceptance note names shape (a) alone; add shape (b) in the body or the carried commit.
13. **Cost.** `claimedByBooks` runs one `resolveBookTree` per registered book per tree request, now also on the `allReadable` fast path (previously zero audience passes there). Linear in books × docs × groups over a docs corpus; acceptable for this route, noted for the record.
14. **Test hygiene (cosmetic).** `rest.test.ts:797` `rest.registerRoutes();` is indented two spaces inside a six-space block. `Lint · ESLint` on the head is `success`, so the lint of record accepts it; fix in the carried commit if convenient.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27091-book-tree-sibling-claims.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`. The diff moves src in exactly those two published packages (`packages/spec/package.json` and `packages/rest/package.json`, both 18.1.0, neither `private`); no other published package's src moves (the test, liveness and changeset files publish nothing). Every published package whose src moves is named, at the right level — **right**.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — **true**: no key, accepted value, default or meaning an author can write changes; a rendered tree's catch-all shrinks. `none` ⇒ `patch` per the Post-Task Checklist level table.
- `Clause-②: no` — **true**: no accept set widens or narrows, no export is added or removed; the one public-surface change is an optional trailing parameter on an existing export, source- and binary-compatible for every existing call. The PR body and the changeset body both carry the two declaration lines at line start, identical.
- No `@object-ui/*` changeset at this head, correctly: no `ui/` file moves at `bce03897`. The carried console commit will owe one `@object-ui/console: patch` line (the amendment orders it) — a carried item, not a defect of this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`** in os-dev-report 6470190013 — none to answer.
- **Dev flag: console port left as is (class a).** Answered in ①9. The seat's amendment 6470220479 orders `book-nav.ts` fixed in THIS PR, so the state at this head is recorded as **carried, not a FAIL**: at `bce03897` the port still judges per book; `DocPage.tsx:165` and `BookPage.tsx:52` still call it with two arguments; `useBookData().authoredBooks` exists (`use-book-data.ts:25`) to be passed. The carried commit must: add the same optional fourth `books` argument to the port's `resolveBookTree` with the same shrink-only orphan filter; have `DocPage`/`BookPage` pass `authoredBooks` (never the portal set — its implicit per-package books would claim docs with no `packageId`); keep the port's line-18 "faithful local port" sentence true; pin it with the console's test surface (a parity pin against `@objectstack/spec`'s `resolveBookTree`, as `book-nav.uncategorizedScope-11340.test.ts` does); add one `@object-ui/console` patch changeset. That commit re-opens this review on its new head.
- **Dev flag: `?package=` scope note.** Answered in ①12: acceptable; should-fix the body note to name the group-level `package` shape too.
- **Dev flag: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally.** Measured in CI by the required `Build Core` context (ci.yml job `build-core`, step `run: pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, after the build that produces every `dist`; the ci.yml paths filter lists `scripts/check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs` for that job). Conclusion on the head: `Build Core` completed `success`, so the gate is measured green in CI.
- **Dev flag: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exit 3 then 0** (shallow clone lacked the pinned fixture). Covered by `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head: completed `success` (its `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` leg `success`).
- **Check-runs on `bce03897`, read to completion.** Required contexts per `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` on `origin/main` `0cd578f7` (and identically at the merge-base `d745bb5e`): TEN — the brief's nine plus `Live E2E UI`, added by #27154. All 49 check-runs completed at 13:45Z; the PR head was still `bce03897` at that read. Conclusions: `Lint & Repo Gates` success · `TypeScript Type Check` success · `Test Core` success (8/8 shards success) · `Build Core` success · `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success · `Lint UI` **skipped** — by design: ci.yml `lint-ui` runs only when `needs.filter.outputs.ui` fires and no `ui/` path is in this diff (a skipped required context passes the ruleset) · `Build & E2E UI` success · `Type Check UI` success · `Test UI` success (aggregate; the 16-shard matrix skipped as planned) · `Live E2E UI` success. Every other completed check is `success` or a by-design `skipped` (Dogfood matrix, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, the opt-in harnesses, the schedule gate); none is `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`.
- **Author:** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay-author note owed. PR assignee `os-support-ai` mirrors the card's.
- **Branch name:** `claude/project-thread-oe80gc`, not `claude/issue-27091-*`; the claim 6468704954 records it as measured (the thread's platform-assigned branch). `PR-body guards` is `success`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e4a5898dee9d3f85b3756d01867501bcdcd50e5c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts + ui/apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/DocPage.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/BookPage.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.siblingBooks-27091.test.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/use-book-data.ts (`toBook`, `authoredBooks`, `buildPortalBooks` consumer), ui/apps/console/src/pages/DocsSlug.tsx (`homeBook`), .changeset/27091-book-tree-sibling-claims.md, packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/doc.json, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts

Round 2 on the same brief. Round 1 (record 6470694256) passed `bce03897`; this round judges the delta `bce03897`...`e4a5898d` — two commits, `7f1a2b23` (console port) and `e4a5898d` (one indent in `rest.test.ts`) — plus the re-written PR body, against GitHub (PR object, file list, delta diff, the head's check-runs read to completion), card #27091 (body and its four comments, no new comment since round 1), ADR-0046 §6.4 and §6.7, #20980. Head at review start = PR head `e4a5898d`; no later commits.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The spec half I passed is unmoved — right.** The delta touches nothing under `packages/spec/src`, `packages/spec/liveness` or `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`; its only `packages/**` hunk is the indent of `rest.test.ts:798` (`rest.registerRoutes();`, two → six spaces; whitespace only). Every round-1 judgment on `resolveBookTree`, `claimsPerBook`, `resolveDocAudiences`, `readableTree` and the liveness quote stands on this head, and the `Spec property liveness` check-run is `success`.
2. **Console port `book-nav.ts` `resolveBookTree(book, docs, bookPackage?, books?)` — additive, right.** Optional trailing parameter typed `readonly Book[]`; the five remaining in-file 2-argument calls (`countBookDocs`, `findBookContainingDoc`, `claimedByBooks`'s own recursion-free call, the `firstDoc` path before BookPage's edit, tests) compile and answer as before. `@object-ui/console` is an app package, not a type-surface consumers import from; no api-surface artifact exists for it.
3. **Shrink-only orphan filter in the port — right.** The one behavioural edit is the same extra conjunct as the spec's: `!claimed.has(d.name) && !claimedByAnyBook?.has(d.name)`, before the unchanged #20980 own-packages scope test; nothing is added to any group. Without `books`, `claimedByAnyBook` is `undefined` and the predicate is the pre-PR one (the new test's CONTROL case pins the admin pages still under *Uncategorized* without `books`).
4. **`claimedByBooks` — a mirror of `resolveBookClaimedDocs`, judged acceptable, with its drift bounded by a parity pin.** It is a second hand-written claim judge, but so is every line of this file: the header declares the file "a faithful local port" that must work without depending on the published `@objectstack/spec` version or the tree endpoint (its reason to exist), and the port already carried its own per-book claim reading in `countBookDocs` and `findBookContainingDoc` (both skip `g.synthetic`). The new helper follows that house shape: `resolveBookTree(book, docs)` per book (scope falls to `bookPackage ?? book.packageId`, which is what the spec's `claimsPerBook` reads as `book.packageId`), skip the synthetic group, union the `doc` entries. No recursion: the inner call passes no `books`. The one reading that differs from the spec's: the spec drops the group keyed `uncategorized` by KEY, the port drops the synthetic group by FLAG, so an authored group an author literally keys `uncategorized` is "claimed" in the port and "unclaimed" in the spec — a pre-existing divergence of the port (its `countBookDocs` has judged by flag since objectui#11340), at a corner no fixture exercises, and the port's reading is the stricter one. **Parity pin present:** test 1 of `book-nav.siblingBooks-27091.test.tsx` asserts, for each HotCRM book, the port's tree with `authored` equals `@objectstack/spec/system`'s `resolveBookTree` with the same docs and the same books (shaped `{ name, label, groups, packageId }`) — the answer the tree route serves. The two judges cannot drift apart on the fixture without that pin going red.
5. **"Faithful local port" is true again — right.** The header sentence (line 18) and the docblock's "Faithful port of ADR-0046 §6.2.1" describe a resolver that now carries the same four parameters and the same orphan rule as the spec's; the docblock states the new rule, cites §6.4 and #27091, and says to pass the AUTHORED books, never the portal set, with the reason (implicit per-package books are a reading fallback, not an authored claim). Each sentence matches the code read.
6. **`DocPage.tsx:168` and `BookPage.tsx:52` pass `useBookData().authoredBooks` — right, and never the portal set.** Both destructure `authoredBooks` beside `books`, resolve the book found in the portal set (`books`, the slug lookup, unchanged) and judge with `authoredBooks`; both `useMemo` dependency arrays gained `authoredBooks`. `use-book-data.ts:92` builds `authoredBooks` from `meta.getItems('book')` through `toBook` (stamping `packageId: it._packageId ?? it.packageId`), and `books` separately as `buildPortalBooks(authoredBooks, docs)`. Had the portal set been passed, `buildPortalBooks`'s implicit books (`include: '*'`, `package: p`) would claim every doc of their package including ones with no `packageId` (`matchesInclude` admits an unstamped doc into every scope) — the trap the amendment named; it is avoided. The viewed book being itself implicit (no authored book for its package) is unaffected: its `include: '*'` group already claims every doc, so its catch-all was empty before.
7. **The port's other 2-argument callers — unaffected, right.** `countBookDocs` (book-card doc counts) and `findBookContainingDoc` (`homeBook`, `DocsSlug.tsx:114`) read authored groups only (`!g.synthetic`), so the catch-all never reaches their answer; `homeBook`'s fallback `ownBooks[0]` is unchanged. `BookPage`'s `firstDoc(resolveBookTree(found, docs, undefined, authoredBooks))` now prefers an `*_index` doc, else the first authored entry, over a tree without a sibling's pages in the catch-all — the right opening page, and a change only when a book has no authored docs at all.
8. **The new console test pins the HotCRM fixture — right.** `crm_manual` + `crm_admin_manual` over package `crm`, disjoint includes, four docs: (1) neither port tree has an `uncategorized` group AND each equals the spec resolver's answer with the same books; (2) `crm_stray` (no book claims it) still rolls up; (3) CONTROL without `books`; (4) `DocPage` rendered at `/docs/crm_manual/crm_overview` through `BookDataContext` with `books: buildPortalBooks(authored, docs)` and `authoredBooks: authored` shows the `Leads` link, no `Uncategorized` text and no link to either admin page — the card's symptom pinned at the rendered sidebar, through the real page. The fixture omits the admin manual's `audience` (the port's `BookAudience` has no `permissionSet` form and the console sidebar does not gate — the REST layer does, round 1 ①7), which does not weaken the placement pin.
9. **Changeset — right.** `'@object-ui/console': patch` added to the existing changeset beside `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/rest`; `@object-ui/console` is published (18.1.0, no `private`), a member of the root `.changeset/config.json` `fixed` group (precedent: `.changeset/25712-renderer-runs-one-sdui-parser.md`), and the body gained one bullet describing the console change truthfully. Both declaration lines unchanged at line start.
10. **PR body `?package=` note — now matches the code.** It names both cross-package shapes that do not judge under `?package=X` (a group carrying `package: X` with an `include`; a group whose `key` an X doc names in its explicit `group`), says unscoped reads judge with every book, and adds that the console reads books unscoped (`use-book-data.ts:86`, `meta.getItems('book')` with no package) so every authored book judges there — all three sentences true against `meta-item-read-routes.ts:395`, `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:1153` and `use-book-data.ts`. Round 1's should-fix is closed.
11. **Round-1 cosmetic — closed.** `rest.test.ts:798` is now indented with its block.
12. **Callers table in the body** still lists the spec callers correctly and now states the console port's state on `bce03897` and its fix in `7f1a2b23` — accurate on this head.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `@object-ui/console: patch` — exactly the three published packages whose src moves on this head (`packages/spec`, `packages/rest`, `ui/apps/console`); no other published package's src moves (the new `.test.tsx` publishes nothing). Every published package named, at the right level — **right**.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — **true** (no key, value, default or meaning an author can write changes); `none` ⇒ `patch` per the Post-Task Checklist level table.
- `Clause-②: no` — **true**: no accept set widens or narrows; no export is added or removed in a published type surface; the console port's optional parameter is on an app-internal module. Present at line start in the PR body and the changeset, identical.

### ③ Boundary flags
